system: civil law system; Constitutional Court review of legislative acts

constitution.history: 14 December 1995 (constitution included as part of the Dayton Peace Accords)
constitution.amend: decided by the Parliamentary Assembly, including a two-thirds majority vote of members present in the House of Representatives; the constitutional article on human rights and fundamental freedoms cannot be amended
constitution.note: each of the political entities has its own constitution

courts.highest: Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH) Constitutional Court (consists of 9 members); Court of BiH (consists of 44 national judges and 7 international judges organized into 3 divisions - Administrative, Appellate, and Criminal, which includes a War Crimes Chamber)
courts.judges: BiH Constitutional Court judges - 4 selected by the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina House of Representatives, 2 selected by the Republika Srpska's National Assembly, and 3 non-Bosnian judges selected by the president of the European Court of Human Rights; Court of BiH president and national judges appointed by the High Judicial and Prosecutorial Council; Court of BiH president appointed for renewable 6-year term; other national judges appointed to serve until age 70; international judges recommended by the president of the Court of BiH and appointed by the High Representative for Bosnia and Herzegovina; international judges appointed to serve until age 70
courts.lower: the Federation has 10 cantonal courts plus a number of municipal courts; the Republika Srpska has a supreme court, 5 district courts, and a number of municipal courts

citizenship.descent: at least one parent must be a citizen of Bosnia and Herzegovina
citizenship.dual: yes, provided there is a bilateral agreement with the other state

suffrage: 18 years of age, 16 if employed; universal
world: has not submitted an ICJ jurisdiction declaration; accepts ICCt jurisdiction
